narrative.overview:
A five-star hotel prepares a suite overnight and hands it back at dawn; IPS does that for whole buildings. The system is built from the material of that ritual: the colour of the sky through an office window across one night shift, a brass key fob, hotel stationery with a ruled border, a room-number plate, and a written list ticked off in order. The page does not decorate the night; it is the night. As the reader scrolls, the ground moves from dusk through midnight to dawn mist and morning linen, and every chapter is stamped with the hour it happens.

Density is calm and editorial: generous section spacing, one idea per viewport, text set in a left column with the hour hanging in a margin ledger beside it. Structure is carried by hairlines rather than boxes. The only objects that leave the page plane are paper ones (the turndown card, the quote form), and they cast the long soft shadow of a card laid on a pillow. Motion is slow, scrubbed by scroll and settles without overshoot; the visitor sets the pace of the night.

The world refuses the cleaning category's blue-and-white crew photo with sparkles, and the safety-sign cartoon register this redesign replaced: no pictograms, no uppercase signage headlines, no bounce, no cream.
keyCharacteristics: The ground colour is the clock: seven hour grounds from dusk (#24304A) to morning linen (#F1F2EE), blended live on scroll.
Ink flips with the ground; text never sits on the wrong side of dusk or dawn.
Brass is the single accent and means "signed off": fob, sign-off ticks, hairline rules.
Tenor Sans in sentence case for headlines; Hanken Grotesk with tabular figures for reading and time.
Hairline ledgers instead of cards; stationery double rules instead of fills.
One long out-ease, no overshoot; light appears only where work happens.

rules.name: The Ground Is the Clock Rule
rules.body: Each chapter declares its hour ground; a scroll script blends between adjacent grounds with a smoothstep over 55% of the viewport, probing at 62% of the viewport height, and paints the result on the root. New chapters take the ground of the hour they depict, in order. Never paint a section a colour outside the hour sequence.

rules.name: The Ink Flips Rule
rules.body: When the live ground's relative luminance passes 0.2, all text, brass-as-text and hairline tokens switch from the dark set (on-dark, brass-hi, light hairline) to the light set (ink, brass-deep, dark hairline), and the nav button swaps to night. Paper objects pin their own ink and never flip.

rules.name: The Signed-Off Brass Rule
rules.body: Brass means one thing: signed off, held or ruled. It appears as a 1px line, a tick, a fob or a ring. It is never a section ground, a button fill or a body-text colour.

rules.name: The Alarm Is Real Rule
rules.body: Alarm red appears only where something is actually wrong. It is never used for emphasis or urgency marketing.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Plate Rule
rules.body: Tenor Sans is set at weight 400, in sentence case, tracked -1.2%, with balanced wrapping. It is never bolded and never set in capitals for headlines; capitals read as signage. The only tracked-capital Tenor settings are the IPS wordmark (0.14em) and client name marks (0.24em).

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time, count and figure uses tabular lining numerals so a moving clock never jitters. Times are written 24-hour, HH:MM.

rules.name: The Label Names Data Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase Hanken labels a field, a column or a value. It never sits above a heading to introduce it; the hour in the margin column does that job.

rules.name: The Paper Object Rule
rules.body: Only things that would be paper in the hotel (a card, a form, a printed specimen) get a shadow, and it is always long, soft and offset downward. Rows, panels, nav and buttons stay flat.

rules.name: The Light Means Work Rule
rules.body: In the 3D floor, all light is warm lamp light (#FFCF94 at rest, warming to #FFA94D while a room is worked) against a cool moonlit ambient. A room lights while its task is active, dims once done, and leaves a small brass ring on the floor as its sign-off. Light never appears as decoration.

dos: **Do** give every new chapter an hour and the ground colour of that hour, in sequence from dusk (#24304A) to morning linen (#F1F2EE).
**Do** hang the hour in the margin column level with the heading, with its brass hairline beneath.
**Do** set headlines in Tenor Sans 400, sentence case, tracked -1.2%.
**Do** set every time and number with tabular lining figures, in 24-hour HH:MM.
**Do** separate content with 1px hairlines and ruled rows; reserve paper fills and shadows for stationery objects.
**Do** draw the stationery double rule on buttons (4px band then 1px brass) and inside paper objects (1px brass, 10px inset).
**Do** move everything on one long out-ease, cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1), over 0.4s for state changes and 1.2 to 1.4s for arrivals; tie scenes to scroll where they tell time.
**Do** let rows and lists change in place: ghost finished steps, slide the ledger, light a tick. Nothing pops in.
**Do** honour reduced motion: drop transitions, show revealed content immediately, and render the 3D floor statically on scroll.
donts: **Don't** use brass as a fill for sections or buttons, or as a body-text colour; it is a line, a tick, a fob or a ring.
**Don't** use cream or any warm off-white ground; the light grounds are cool linen (#F1F2EE) and mist (#C9D6DF).
**Don't** set headlines in capitals or bold.
**Don't** put a tracked uppercase label above a heading as an eyebrow or kicker.
**Don't** use pictograms or illustrative icon sets. The only drawn marks are the fob, the arrow, the tick, the signature and dimensioned spec drawings, all in one line weight.
**Don't** round shapes beyond 2px or use pills; circles are for indicator dots and rings only.
**Don't** bounce, overshoot, spring or loop; things arrive and stay arrived.
**Don't** light the 3D scene, or glow any UI, where no work is happening.
**Don't** use alarm red for anything that is not a real problem.
